source.title: Scaling Distributed Training of Flood-Filling Networks on HPC Infrastructure for Brain Mapping
source.authors: Wu Dong; N. Ferrier; N. Kasthuri; P. Littlewood; Murat Keçeli; Rafael Vescovi; Hanyu Li; Corey Adams; E. Jennings; S. Flender; T. Uram; V. Vishwanath

record.tranche_reason: Applies large-batch training to flood-filling networks for 3D brain-image segmentation and reports training-efficiency and held-out segmentation results.
record.gate_note: Reports a batch-size sweep with training efficiency and F1, and validation segmentation metrics. The cited findings from other studies are not rows. The batch-size results concern efficiency and training performance; the paper does not measure the generalization gap under the claim's natural-label classification setup.
record.test_reason: The study measures batch-size effects on training F1, throughput and training efficiency, not held-out performance under matched epoch budgets. Its held-out segmentation evaluation uses one batch-size configuration and compares different methods. These results do not test V5 or any other listed version; claims about large-batch generalization are cited background.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors report scaling to 2048 KNL nodes, similar segmentation performance to prior methods with shorter training time, and batch-size choices that balance acceleration against declining training efficiency. They also report a shift from linear toward square-root optimal learning-rate scaling as batch size increases.
record.recipe_differences: Uses synchronous data-parallel SGD infrastructure, but trains an FFN for 3D electron-microscopy segmentation; batch-size analysis focuses on training efficiency and training F1 rather than held-out generalization error.
record.method_sensitivity: Batch size changes training efficiency; optimal learning rates shift from linear scaling at smaller node counts toward square-root scaling as batch size increases. Throughput also varies with MPI ranks, thread counts, TensorFlow environment, and KMP_BLOCKTIME.

fits_no_version.finding: Larger batches shorten wall time to a target training F1 with diminishing gains, while smaller batches use processed FOVs more efficiently.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: FFN batch size trades training speed against training efficiency per processed example.

fits_no_version.finding: A distributed FFN run achieved validation ARE 0.1074 and VOI 1.9518; comparisons with published segmentation methods vary by metric.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Distributed FFN training can produce competitive held-out segmentation scores.

record.problems: The batch-size figures provide no numerical values in the text and assess training F1/efficiency rather than held-out error. The validation comparison reports segmentation metrics for one stated run, without uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional eligible results left out. Figures 3–6 concern throughput or learning-rate selection; cited results are prior work and are not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and corresponding natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons of held-out performance.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets, and whether recipe adaptations remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout effects on held-out error and interactions with data size, augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: No verdict labels are warranted. Neither the single-configuration validation results nor the statement that FFNs do not easily overfit supplies the missing controlled comparison for V5.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test generalization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance.
No fixed-epoch comparison of held-out performance between batch sizes; the study reports training efficiency and training F1, and uses validation segmentation metrics in a separate run.
Sharpness or other measured properties tracking the generalization gap.

rows.value: Training efficiency degrades with batch size; precise values figure only
rows.note: The text explicitly describes degradation; plotted batch-specific values are not provided numerically. This is training efficiency, not held-out error.
rows.check: Training efficiency to F1 0.3 cannot establish a batch-size effect on held-out performance. The reported decline is an optimization-efficiency finding, not partial evidence for V5.

rows.subject: FFN
rows.size_stated: 12 modules; 32 output features per convolutional layer
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated trained FFN segmentation on a validation subvolume distinct from the training subvolume.
rows.measure: Adapted Rand error (ARE) and variation of information (VOI)
rows.note: These segmentation scores are compared with other methods, but do not report a train-test error gap or a batch-size effect on held-out error.
rows.check: The validation scores are correctly reported, but evaluate the study's own method without a controlled batch-size comparison. This should not be an evidence row for any listed version. The effective global batch size is 8192: 8 per node across 1024 nodes.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
